subject: Hosted API: Commit proposal & procurement form request
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing proposal + commit tiers (follow-up from demo)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Per our convo, I've put together a simple committed-tier proposal that should materially lower your per-token unit cost for predictable usage while keeping hosted API flexibility:

- No-commit (on-demand): $0.000600 per token
- 12-month commit tiers (true-up quarterly):
  - 0–100M tokens / month: $0.000600 (no discount)
  - 100M–500M tokens / month: 12% discount -> $0.000528 per token
  - 500M+ tokens / month: 20% discount -> $0.000480 per token

We typically invoice monthly against committed usage with a quarterly true-up. For procurement friendliness, we can provide:
- Line-item pricing by token band for your PO
- An onboarding credit ($10,000 one-time) applied against the first invoice for 12-month commitments >= 300M tokens

Next steps: if the bands above look reasonable, please send your PO requirements and/or your preferred vendor form. I can route the vendor form to legal for review, and we can convert to an MSA + appendix if that’s preferred.

Happy to hop on a short call with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0114
[attachment: Commit_Tiers_Appendix.pdf (PDF, 128 KB)]

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecorp.com
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing proposal + commit tiers (follow-up from demo)

Rafael,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the appendix. A few procurement items before we advance to commercial:

1) We require our standard preferred vendor form to be executed for any new vendors. I attached the form — please review and return.
2) Our finance team requires net45 payment terms on vendor invoices; we will issue a PO referencing the executed vendor form.
3) Can you provide a simple billing breakdown (line items) showing baseline committed spend vs variable overage? Finance needs that on the PO.
4) We need SOC 2 Type II attestation and confirmation of data residency controls (we process EU PII and would like EU data residency if possible).
5) One more ask: procurement prefers fixed pricing within a term rather than a variable per-token rate. We need language on a guaranteed price for the committed tier period.

Please note I sent the vendor form to vendor_management@acmecorp.com as well.

Elena Rossi
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Corp
[attachment: Acme_Preferred_Vendor_Form.pdf (PDF, 245 KB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmecorp.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 17:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing proposal + commit tiers (follow-up from demo)

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Quick answers and proposed path forward:

- Vendor form: we can review and sign, but will need a quick legal review before execution. Please confirm preferred return method (DocuSign or signed PDF).
- Net45: we typically run net30 for self-serve customers but for enterprise accounts we can accept net45 on a committed contract with an executed vendor form and PO.
- Billing breakdown: attaching an invoice-friendly sample with committed line-item + overage band math (Commit_Tiers_Appendix.pdf).
- Fixed pricing during the committed term: yes — we can lock the per-token rate for the term. For transparency I propose we lock the per-token rate for the 12-month commit and allow quarterly true-ups only to reconcile actual usage against committed minimums.
- SOC 2 & data residency: we can provide SOC 2 Type II and discuss EU-region hosting for data residency; I'll loop in our security team if required.

If acceptable, next step from your side is to confirm: (A) desired commit size and term length, (B) return method for the vendor form, and (C) PO lead / billing contact. I will route to legal for a quick vendor-form review.

Thanks,
Rafael
[attachment: Commit_Tiers_Appendix.xlsx (XLSX, 42 KB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme procurement pushback — vendor form + net45 request

Marissa / Connor —

Looping you both in for quick guidance. Acme wants (a) our signed preferred vendor form, (b) net45 payment terms, (c) fixed pricing for the committed term. They indicated SOC 2 and EU data residency as gating items.

My proposed commercial move: offer a 12-month commit at 300M tokens/month (they expect bursty traffic) with the following tweaks:
- Lock per-token price for 12 months (no mid-term price changes)
- Apply our 12% commit discount band + an additional one-time commercial 5% off the applicable per-token rate to win the deal
- Convert onboarding credit to $7,000 (approved as a concession)
- Accept net45 for this enterprise deal if legal okays the vendor form and liability language

Question: are we OK to accept net45 and to have legal sign the Acme vendor PDF after review? Also confirm the extra 5% ad hoc discount and $7k onboarding credit. If yes I will present to Acme with a signed vendor form route (DocuSign).

—Rafael

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme procurement pushback — vendor form + net45 request

Rafael —

Thanks for the summary. Guidance below:

- Approve net45 for enterprise commitments; we prefer net30 but net45 is acceptable on a case-by-case basis.
- Approve the one-time 5% commercial concession on top of the existing commit discount for a 12-month, 300M token/month commitment.
- Approve $7,000 onboarding credit (please mark as one-time non-recurring credit).
- Legal: do not sign any third-party vendor PDF without our Legal review. Send the Acme PDF to legal@redwood.com with a short note and proposed minimal redlines: liability cap (1x fees), IP carveouts, data residency clause, and indemnity scope. If legal signs off, we can return via DocuSign.
- Security: confirm SOC 2 Type II attestation and provide EU-region hosting details (we can offer Frankfurt region).

If you want I will loop Lauren for executive sign-off on the net45 exception once Legal gives the all-clear.

Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
